sources.title: PRISMA 2020 Statement
appraisalNotes: Research-process guidance, not hospitality outcome evidence.
Reporting completeness does not by itself guarantee review quality.

sources.title: PRISMA Extension for Scoping Reviews (PRISMA-ScR)
sources.populationOrScope: Scoping-review reporting across broad evidence fields
appraisalNotes: Maps the breadth of the initial cross-disciplinary Library.
Targeted systematic reviews remain necessary for consequential disputed claims.

sources.title: Cochrane Handbook for Systematic Reviews of Interventions, Version 6.5
sources.populationOrScope: Systematic-review planning, conduct, bias appraisal and interpretation
appraisalNotes: Methods are adapted because StayOpti is not a clinical intervention review.
Relevant to bias, indirectness, missing evidence and updates.

sources.title: GRADE Handbook and official GRADE approach
sources.populationOrScope: Certainty of evidence and recommendation formulation
appraisalNotes: StayOpti adapts certainty concepts, not clinical starting grades or thresholds.
Certainty attaches to a claim/outcome in context.

sources.title: Evidence-to-Decision Tables
sources.populationOrScope: Structured movement from evidence to contextual decisions
appraisalNotes: Supports explicit desirable/undesirable effects, values, resources, acceptability and feasibility.
Domain-specific StayOpti criteria require independent evidence.

sources.title: WHO Guide for Evidence-Informed Decision-Making
sources.populationOrScope: Identification, appraisal and mobilization of evidence for decisions
appraisalNotes: Supports separation between evidence appraisal and recommendation judgment.
Not used to infer traveler preferences.

sources.title: Artificial Intelligence Risk Management Framework (AI RMF 1.0)
authorsOrInstitution: National Institute of Standards and Technology
sources.populationOrScope: Risk management and trustworthy AI lifecycle governance
appraisalNotes: Supports validity, reliability, safety, transparency, explainability, privacy and fairness governance.
Does not prescribe ranking weights.

sources.title: Artificial Intelligence Risk Management Framework: Generative AI Profile
authorsOrInstitution: National Institute of Standards and Technology
sources.populationOrScope: Generative-AI information integrity and risk controls
appraisalNotes: Supports provenance, fact/opinion/inference separation and uncertainty acknowledgment.
Language generation remains downstream of deterministic evidence.

sources.title: Hotelstars Union Classification Criteria 2025–2030
sources.populationOrScope: Official hotel classification criteria in participating European systems
appraisalNotes: Establishes category/service expectations only where classification provenance matches.
Does not prove experienced quality or global cross-country equivalence.

sources.title: ISO 21902:2021 — Accessible tourism for all
sources.populationOrScope: Requirements and recommendations for equal access and enjoyment of tourism
appraisalNotes: Accessibility is a hard fit requirement when declared, not a generic comfort bonus.
Full text requires licensed access; only legal extracts/metadata are stored.

sources.title: UN Tourism Accessible Tourism Publications and Guidelines
sources.populationOrScope: Accessible tourism across the end-to-end tourism value chain
appraisalNotes: Supports evaluating property, information, transport and experience as a chain.
Individual needs remain explicit hard requirements.

sources.title: Web Content Accessibility Guidelines (WCAG) 2.2
sources.populationOrScope: Testable web-content accessibility requirements and guidance
appraisalNotes: Applies to presentation and interaction, not property accessibility scoring.
Automated checks do not replace human evaluation.

sources.title: Directive (EU) 2019/882 — European Accessibility Act
sources.populationOrScope: EU accessibility requirements for covered products and services
appraisalNotes: Legal applicability requires separate legal assessment.
Supports accessible information and transaction design.
